items.label: 1B
items.claim: UCLA's cheaper X Plus flow-cell tiers were cut 19-29% per lane between the 2023-24 sheets and the 1 Jul 2026 page, so repricing inside the X family is large and dated.
items.detail: The tier prices below are the 2024 sheet's external non-profit column versus the 2026 page's single external column. The two columns are assumed comparable; the 2026 page does not define its column. 10B-300 fell $2,234 to $1,765.67 (-21.0%), 10B-200 $2,109 to $1,665.53 (-21.0%) and 10B-100 $1,798 to $1,457.26 (-18.9%). 1.5B-300 fell $3,307 to $2,338.81 (-29.3%), 1.5B-200 $3,014 to $2,189.40 (-27.4%) and 1.5B-100 $2,433 to $1,874.17 (-23.0%). The Aug 2023 and Mar 2024 sheets had identical X Plus prices, so the whole cut came after Mar 2024.
items.source_name: UCLA TCGB rate sheets (Mar 2024 PDF, Jul 2026 page)
items.why_new: Known data only had UCLA's 25B-300 at $3.51; the 10B and 1.5B lane cuts versus 2024 are new.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: At UCLA the premium of 10B over 25B per read shrank from about 58% to about 26% because 10B was cut and 25B was held.
items.detail: Assuming lane output scales with flow-cell cluster count (25B:10B = 1:0.4), 10B-300 cost (2,234/0.4)/3,538 = 1.58x the 25B per unit of output in the 2024 sheet. On the 2026 page it costs (1,765.67/0.4)/3,512.47 = 1.26x. The lane-output assumption is mine, not UCLA's. Equivalently, the 25B discount per Gb versus 10B narrowed from about -37% to about -20%. The 25B price barely moved while the 10B price fell, so the within-X price ladder has been flattened by cuts to the lower tiers.
items.why_new: Known data had the 10B to 25B step at -24% to -37% per Gb at cores; UCLA's own time series shows it narrowing as the 10B tier reprices.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: UCLA's 25B-300 lane price was essentially unchanged across nearly three years, which cuts against fast discounting on the flagship flow cell at this core.
items.detail: The external non-profit price was $3,538 in Aug 2023 and again in Mar 2024 (the 6/18/2024 revision is identical), and is $3,512.47 on the 1 Jul 2026 page (-0.7%). Internal 25B-300 was $3,168 in 2023-24. Core rates are pass-through plus labor and policy, not Illumina's net price. Library prep at the same core rose over the period: stranded mRNA prep $63 to $68.14 (+8%), DNA prep $61 to $68.90 (+13%).
items.why_new: This is a three-point time series for the 25B at one major core; the 25B-300 was known only as a $3.51 snapshot.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: UCLA's core dropped every NovaSeq 6000 line (SP, S1, S2, S4) within about 7 months of Aug 2023, so research-core conversion was already complete by early 2024.
items.detail: The Aug 2023 sheet lists SP, S1, S2 and S4 lanes plus a 6000 XP loading fee. The 1 Mar 2024 sheet (and the 6/18/2024 revision) lists only X Plus 1.5B, 10B and 25B lanes. The 1 Jul 2026 page also shows no 6000. A tail at a major research core ended well before the 2026 'substantially done' claim, which supports the view that the remaining 6000 volume is clinical and not research.
items.source_name: UCLA TCGB rate sheets (Aug 2023 vs Mar 2024)
items.why_new: Dated retirement of the 6000 at a named large academic core, with before/after sheets; known items had only anecdotal retirements.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The 6000 lane price at UCLA fell 10-16% from Jul 2022 to Aug 2023, before the 6000 was withdrawn, so list-price erosion on the 6000 started well before conversion.
items.detail: Internal S4-300 went $5,356.20 to $4,817 (-10.1%) and SP-300 $2,765.55 to $2,406 (-13.0%). S1-300 went $4,069.50 to $3,719 (-8.6%) and S2-300 $6,655.35 to $6,407 (-3.7%). External S4-300 was $6,014.15 in 2022 and $5,057 non-profit in 2023 (-15.9%); the 2022 external column may not match the 2023 non-profit column. Cuts came while X was still new, consistent with 6000 pricing being pushed down.
items.why_new: Known 6000 list cuts were Salk and EPFL; this is a 2022-23 UCLA series for all four 6000 flow cells.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: On Aug 2023 UCLA rates the 6000 S4 lane cost about 1.9x the X Plus 25B lane per Gb, and the 1.5B X lane was priced above the SP lane.
items.detail: Taking spec yields of ~750 Gb per S4 lane (3 Tb over 4 lanes) and ~1 Tb per 25B lane, S4-300 at $5,057 gives $6.74/Gb against 25B-300 at $3,538 giving $3.54/Gb (ratio 1.9x). Yield figures are my approximations. Against the 10B-300 ($2,234 per ~375 Gb = $5.96/Gb) the S4 premium is only about 13%. So the 25B, not the 10B, carried the large per-Gb price gap that drives conversion drag.
items.why_new: Gives a same-core 6000-vs-X per-Gb ratio at a point in time; known 3.4x is the revenue-per-Gb ratio on Illumina's own data.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: UCLA's price for rival MGI DNBseq T7 flow cells fell 36-37% between the Mar 2024 sheet and the Jul 2026 page.
items.detail: T7-300 fell from $4,736 to $3,043 (-35.7%), T7-200 from $4,248 to $2,688.95 (-36.7%), and T7-150 now lists at $3,651.20. These are the 2024 non-profit and 2026 external columns. The same core's Nanopore GridION run fell $2,644 to $1,951.33 (-26%). A university core is therefore passing through falling low-cost-rival run prices while the Illumina 25B stayed flat.
items.why_new: Known MGI evidence was unit counts and a T7+ cost claim; this is a priced time series at a US core.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: UCLA Illumina X Plus lane-price cuts of ~20-29% on 10B and 1.5B hit a research-heavy core, while its non-sequencing items rose or were mixed.
items.detail: UCLA's own 10X 3' GEX fresh prep fell $2,093 to $1,810.81 (-13.5%). Visium HD rose $6,977 to $7,725 (+10.7%), and MiSeq v3 PE150 fell $1,814 to $1,791 (-1.2%). Sequencing lines on the Illumina X tiers fell most. This suggests the research buyer base sees larger per-run reductions on Illumina's X flow cells than on other services.
items.why_new: No prior comparison of UCLA 2024 vs 2026 lines; this contrasts X-lane cuts with other services.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: UCLA now carries a 5B lane and a 25B-100 lane at tiered prices, adding more X price points that make cheaper capacity available to research buyers.
items.detail: New 2026 lines are 5B-100/200/300 at $1,210.42/$1,351.61/$1,462.87 per lane, 25B-100 at $2,164.94 and 25B-200 at $3,202.38. The 2024 sheet had only 25B-300. Per unit of output (assuming 5B = 0.2 of a 25B lane), the 5B-300 costs about 2.1x the 25B and the 10B about 1.26x, so the 25B stays the cheapest per Gb. Added mid-size SKUs let smaller research projects move to X at lower ticket price.
items.why_new: Gives the full UCLA 5B/25B-100/25B-200 ladder; only the 25B-300 was known.

notes: Decoded Jul 2022, Aug 2023 and Mar 2024 sheets via the files WebFetch saved, using the Read tool. The 6/18/2024 revision was not re-read but search snippets say it matches Mar 2024. No 2025 sheet was found. The 2026 internal and JCCC rate columns sit in a Box link that was not opened, so the 2026 external column cannot be reconciled with certainty to the 2024 non-profit column. The sheets carry no flow-cell yields, so per-Gb figures use my spec assumptions. Mining is largely exhausted.
